current_activity: lands over the Ouistreham beaches; reaches the airborne area east of the Orne in the afternoon
notes: Event date: 6 June 1944 (Stacey, p. 117: "In the afternoon of D Day"). Event definition: The commandos of the brigade, under Brigadier Lord Lovat, land over the Ouistreham beaches (Queen Red, the easternmost sector of Sword), No. 4 Commando clearing targets in Ouistreham; in the afternoon they reach the 6th Airborne Division's area and start mopping up the coast defences east of the Orne (Stacey, p. 117; Wikipedia). Event support: two source families (Stacey, the Canadian official history, and Wikipedia). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 117: "In the afternoon of D Day the commandos of the 1st Special Service Brigade, commanded by Brigadier Lord Lovat, which had landed over the Ouistreham beaches, arrived in the airborne troops"; Wikipedia, 1st Special Service Brigade: "to land at Ouistreham in Queen Red sector (the most easterly)"; "moving inland to join-up with the 6th Airborne Division". Location: Ouistreham, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Ouistreham; the brigade landed on the beaches by it and moved inland east of the Orne the same afternoon. Location support: Stacey names the Ouistreham beaches (p. 117); Wikipedia names Queen Red sector at Ouistreham. Commander: Brigadier The Lord Lovat, wounded 12 June 1944; then Brigadier Derek Mills-Roberts (Wikipedia, 1st Special Service Brigade; Stacey, p. 117). Context: Relationship: under the 6th Airborne Division from its arrival in the airborne area (Stacey, p. 117; Ellis, vol. I, p. 448 lists the brigade with the division in August); start = row date (inferred value). I Corps as the corps of the 6th Airborne Division (inferred value).

current_activity: Blackcock: under the 7th Armoured Division, clears the country along the Maas north of Echt
notes: Event date: about 20 January 1945 (approximate: Ellis, vol. II, p. 245 gives no day; the 7th Armoured Division was about Echt from 18 January, p. 243, and was bombed in for Montfort on 22 January, p. 246). Event definition: Back from England, the brigade (renamed the 1st Commando Brigade) comes under the 7th Armoured Division from VIII Corps during Operation Blackcock; the division sweeps north-east from Echt while the commandos clear the country next to the Maas (Ellis, vol. II, p. 245). Wikipedia says the brigade was temporarily under the 7th Armoured Division and names Brachterbeek, where Lance Corporal Harden of No. 45 (Royal Marine) Commando won a posthumous Victoria Cross. Event support: two source families (Ellis, the British official history, and Wikipedia). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 245: "With the (renamed) 1st Commando Brigade? coming under its command from VIII Corps"; "while the Commandos cleared the country that adjoined the river Maas"; Wikipedia, 1st Special Service Brigade: "the Brigade took part in Operation Blackcock, and was temporarily placed under command of the 7th Armoured Division"; "This all happened in the little town of Brachterbeek, in the province of Limburg, Netherlands". Location: Brachterbeek, Maasgouw, Limburg (NL) (new place) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Brachterbeek, on the Maas north of Echt; the brigade cleared the river country there. Location support: Wikipedia names Brachterbeek; Ellis names the country by the Maas north of Echt (p. 245). Commander: Brigadier Derek Mills-Roberts, commander from 12 June 1944 (Wikipedia, 1st Special Service Brigade). Context: Event date is approximate (inferred value: no source read gives the day), hence 0.3. Relationship: attached to the 7th Armoured Division, which was in XII Corps for Blackcock (Ellis, vol. II, p. 246); the brigade came from VIII Corps (p. 245); starts = row date (inferred value). The 1944 relations closed on 8 September 1944, when the brigade returned to England (Wikipedia).

current_activity: under the 52nd Division, patrols enter Well on the Maas
notes: Event date: 3 March 1945 (Stacey, p. 514: "Well on the 3rd"). Event definition: On the extreme right of Veritable, fast-moving patrols of the brigade, operating under the 52nd Division, enter Langstraat on 2 March and Well on the 3rd, and next day make contact with the US 17th Cavalry Reconnaissance Squadron in Walbeck (Stacey, p. 514); Ellis says the 52nd Division left its newly joined commando brigade to strike up the Maas valley (vol. II, p. 274). Event support: two source families (Ellis, the British official history, and Stacey, the Canadian official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 274: "Leaving its newly joined 1st Commando Brigade to strike up the Maas valley"; Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 514: "fast-moving patrols of the 1st Commando Brigade, operating under the 52nd Division, entered Langstraat on the 2nd and Well on the 3rd". Location: Well, Bergen, Limburg (NL) (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the village, which the brigade's patrols entered. Location support: Stacey names Well (p. 514). Commander: Brigadier Derek Mills-Roberts, commander from 12 June 1944 (Wikipedia, 1st Special Service Brigade). Context: Relationship: attached to the 52nd Division (Stacey, p. 514; Ellis, vol. II, p. 274), which was in XXX Corps; starts = row date (inferred value).

current_activity: crosses the Rhine about two miles downstream of Wesel and attacks the town after the bombing
notes: Event date: 23 March 1945, from 10 p.m. (Stacey, p. 535; Ellis, vol. II, p. 289: an hour after the 51st Division's assault). Event definition: An hour after the 51st Division's assault, the brigade of XII Corps crosses the Rhine about two miles downstream of Wesel, beginning at 10 p.m., with one commando in Buffaloes forming a bridgehead and another by stormboat leading the assault on Wesel, which Bomber Command then hits with about 1,100 tons of bombs (Ellis, vol. II, p. 289; Stacey, p. 535); Wikipedia puts the crossing about 1.5 km north of Wesel. Event support: three source families (Ellis, the British official history, and Stacey, the Canadian official history, and Wikipedia). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 289: "the 1st Commando Brigade of XII Corps crossed about two miles downstream of Wesel"; Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 535: "the 1st Commando Brigade established itself immediately west of Wesel, beginning its crossing at 10:00 p.m."; Wikipedia, 1st Special Service Brigade: "then the 1st Commando Brigade, 1.5 km north of Wesel". Location: Wesel, North Rhine-Westphalia (PL0632) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the town; the brigade crossed just downstream of it and attacked into it. Location support: Ellis and Stacey place the crossing just downstream (west) of Wesel and the assault on the town. Commander: Brigadier Derek Mills-Roberts, commander from 12 June 1944 (Wikipedia, 1st Special Service Brigade). Context: Relationship: XII Corps (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 285 and 289); start = row date (inferred value); the 52nd Division attachment closed the day before.
